A relative answers and later says the number is not the customer's (or the reverse).

data.question: A relative answers and later says the number is not the customer's (or the reverse).
data.chosen: wrong_number only on an explicit statement that the number does not belong to the customer; 'not here / not available' is the callback path; after a booked callback the close is callback.
data.rationale: Rule 8's trigger is an explicit statement; a booked callback is already in the ledger.

message: 'This <weekday>' already past, a bare weekday, or a weekday equal to today.

data.question: 'This <weekday>' already past, a bare weekday, or a weekday equal to today.
data.chosen: Weeks run Monday to Sunday. A past 'this <weekday>' is before today: say so and ask for a day from today on (a date proposal, not a refusal). A bare weekday is its next occurrence after today. The read-back states weekday and date.
data.rationale: Rule 22 defines only 'this' and 'next'; rule 19 forbids past dates; the read-back is the safety net.

message: Is 'not today, maybe later' or 'when I get paid' a vague period or a flat refusal?

data.question: Is 'not today, maybe later' or 'when I get paid' a vague period or a flat refusal?
data.chosen: Any time reference (a period, an event, 'later') is a vague period: ask once for the exact day, then propose the deadline. A 'no' with no time reference and no amount is a flat refusal.
data.rationale: Rule 29: a proposed date is never a refusal; rule 30 defines a flat refusal as a no with no date and no amount.

message: Restructuring requested after a promise was recorded.

data.question: Restructuring requested after a promise was recorded.
data.chosen: Transfer to the restructuring queue; the recorded promise stays; close transferred / restructuring. Asking to change the recorded promise itself is rule 36 (mobile app).
data.rationale: Rule 41 is unconditional and the closing note says a transfer after a recorded promise closes transferred.

message: Does 'why do you need that?' before a security answer count as declining?

data.question: Does 'why do you need that?' before a security answer count as declining?
data.chosen: Explain once that the questions protect the account and re-ask; close declined only on a second refusal or when the customer again refuses to answer until told the purpose.
data.rationale: The rule says 'instead of answering'; a clarifying question followed by an answer is not a refusal.

message: Brief B says promise wins 'except rule 10' (restructuring); Brief A says any transfer after a recorded promise closes transferred. A support or human transfer after a recorded promise?

data.question: Brief B says promise wins 'except rule 10' (restructuring); Brief A says any transfer after a recorded promise closes transferred. A support or human transfer after a recorded promise?
data.chosen: Any transfer after a recorded promise closes transferred with that transfer's reason.
data.rationale: B-10's last sentence covers all transfers; Brief B does not replace A's transfer rule.

message: Hardship and a request for lower instalments in the same call.

data.question: Hardship and a request for lower instalments in the same call.
data.chosen: Hardship first: sympathy, offer support; accept → support transfer; decline → no_promise / hardship.
data.rationale: Rule 32 comes before rule 41.

message: Does the floor offer use a persuasion attempt, and on which date is it offered?

data.question: Does the floor offer use a persuasion attempt, and on which date is it offered?
data.chosen: 'Too much' to the first ask makes attempt 1 the floor on the attempt-1 date with the rest-stays-overdue sentence; a refused floor is a flat refusal → next attempt (late band: floor on the deadline) or stop.
data.rationale: Rule 30 makes attempt 1 the floor once the full amount was called too much; rule 26 allows attempt 2 to name the floor again on the deadline.

message: days_late outside every band (0, or more than 45).

data.question: days_late outside every band (0, or more than 45).
data.chosen: Use the nearest band and never fail.
data.rationale: The brief scopes calls to 1-45 days late; the agent still has to behave.

message: Attempt-1 date on a weekend call, or after a short deadline.

data.question: Attempt-1 date on a weekend call, or after a short deadline.
data.chosen: When this week's last business day is before today, use next week's; cap any proposal at the deadline.
data.rationale: Rule 19 forbids past dates and dates after the deadline.

message: Callback 'today' on a non-business day; a vague time such as 'in the morning'.

data.question: Callback 'today' on a non-business day; a vague time such as 'in the morning'.
data.chosen: 'Today' is allowed on any day (literal reading); 'later than now' is strict; a vague time is followed by a request for a specific time (not counted as an outside-window offer).
data.rationale: Literal reading of rule 6; rule 7 is the only no-callback path.

message: Amount above the full amount, a floor above the past-due amount, or a missing floor field.

data.question: Amount above the full amount, a floor above the past-due amount, or a missing floor field.
data.chosen: Above the full amount → offer the full amount; effective floor = min(floor, past due); no floor field → no floor offer.
data.rationale: Rule 27 bounds the range at the full amount; rule 33 forbids invented terms.

message: No currency is named in the brief or the tool API.

data.question: No currency is named in the brief or the tool API.
data.chosen: Say amounts with two decimals and no currency word.
data.rationale: Rule 44: never invent facts.

message: 'I don't want to talk' before the right party is confirmed.

data.question: 'I don't want to talk' before the right party is confirmed.
data.chosen: Before right-party confirmation it is an unclear answer (second ask, then not_reached / unclear); after confirmation and before verification it is not_verified / declined.
data.rationale: Rule 45 speaks of 'the same customer'; before confirmation the person is not known to be the customer.

message: A third party will not say when the customer can be reached, or insists on paying.

data.question: A third party will not say when the customer can be reached, or insists on paying.
data.chosen: No disclosure and no payment; without a time no callback is booked → not_reached / no_callback.
data.rationale: Rule 10 forbids any account talk; nothing can be scheduled.

message: A hardship customer declines support but names a date or an amount.

data.question: A hardship customer declines support but names a date or an amount.
data.chosen: Record the promise under the date and amount rules (no persuasion) and close promise; a later accepted support transfer closes transferred / support.
data.rationale: Rule 32's last sentence and the transfer-after-promise note.

message: Notes for a customer with a single product under Brief B.

data.question: Notes for a customer with a single product under Brief B.
data.chosen: Notes apply whenever Brief B is in force, one product included.
data.rationale: B-1 allows one to three products and B-8 applies also when no product gets a promise.

message: When to call add_note, given that a transfer request can come after a dispute or refusal.

data.question: When to call add_note, given that a transfer request can come after a dispute or refusal.
data.chosen: Defer every add_note until the outcome is final (after the last product, with no transfer).
data.rationale: Deferral satisfies B-8/B-9 in the ledger and is the only way to satisfy B-10's no-notes rule.

message: One shared date that is a weekend or holiday, or after every deadline.

data.question: One shared date that is a weekend or holiday, or after every deadline.
data.chosen: Shift first (rule 20), then clamp each product to its own deadline and name every clamped product in the read-back.
data.rationale: Deadlines are business days, so shift-then-clamp never yields a non-business day.

message: The call ends with no situation from the outcome table (e.g. the customer hangs up).

data.question: The call ends with no situation from the outcome table (e.g. the customer hangs up).
data.chosen: Verified customer → no_promise / refused; customer on the line but not verified → not_verified / declined; otherwise not_reached / unclear.
data.rationale: Every call needs exactly one close_call; these rows say the least about the customer.

message: Hardship (customer-level) in a multi-product call when the support offer is declined.

data.question: Hardship (customer-level) in a multi-product call when the support offer is declined.
data.chosen: Make no persuasion attempt on any product; note hardship on every product without a promise and close (no_promise / hardship through the notes rule).
data.rationale: Rule 32 forbids persuasion for the customer; B-8 requires a note for each unpromised product.

message: Wording of the first ask under Brief B for a customer with one product.

data.question: Wording of the first ask under Brief B for a customer with one product.
data.chosen: Several products: ask whether they can pay all of them today; one product: Brief A's 'Can you make this payment today?'.
data.rationale: B-4 generalises A-28; with one product the two coincide.
